newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher boosted by Telebras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher boosted by Telebras.

text.p: Brazil shares ended up 0.7 percent on heavy trading boosted by Telebras, which rose on speculation about a possible telephone rate rise, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares ended up 65 points at 9,302 points. Turnover was heavy at 721 million reais ($680.7 million).
"The market's rise today was heavily concentrated on Telebras whose revenues are likely to grow eight percent if the government announces a rate hike," said Marcio Bressan, broker at Senso brokerage.
Earlier today, Brazil's Telecommunications Minister Sergio Motta said he would hold a news conference at 1830 local/2130 GMT without specifying the subject.
This triggered speculation he would announce a telephone rate increase, which has long been expected by market analysts.
Telebras preferred shares rose 1.5 percent on the speculation to end at 115.10 reais after hitting a high of 115.70 reais during the afternoon session.
Other telecom stocks such as Telesp, Telepar and Telerj also posted strong gains.

Telesp preferred shares ended 3.21 percent higher at 289 reais, while Telerj preferred stock soared 4.79 percent to end at 150.90 reais. Telepar preferred shares jumped 6.77 percent to close at 710 reais.

Brokers said today's rise could also be attributed to an anticipation of Telebras's expected good first quarter results. Analysts expect Telebras to post net earnings of between 800 million reais and 850 million reais in the first three months of the year.
Oil monopoly Petrobras preferred stock fell 0.73 percent to close at 204 reais, while mining giant Vale do Rio Doce dropped 0.6 percent to end at 24.90 reais.
Power firm Eletrobras preferred shares closed at 453 reais, off 0.66 percent.

The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of the nine most liquid power shares rose 1.11 percent to end at 2,534 points. The market's wider Brazil index (IBX) of 100 leading shares also rose, climbing 0.6 percent to close at 1,919 points.
